business_scope.primary_industry_name: Refrigerated Logistics Warehousing for Perishable Pharmaceuticals

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (civil law in Quebec for private law; common law for federal public law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (2012, in force 2014)
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)
Canada–China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1986, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 83.02-83.04 and 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 28; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-45; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-45, r 1; implementing rules on beneficial ownership under FINTRAC reporting guidance and the Canada Business Corporations Act transparency registry (for federal corporations, used by analogy for LP UBO mapping).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-registration or official extract of the proposed limited partnership name
Certified true copy of the general partner’s certificate of existence (if corporate general partner)
Notarized ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and statutory declaration of identity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of residence / Québec notary when executed locally

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or government-issued photo ID for each general partner, limited partner and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or issuing state authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to resident counsel or general partner for pre-incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all named general partners, limited partners, principal contributors, and beneficial owners against: FINTRAC politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations definitions; Global Affairs Canada regional sanctions and consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list; UN Security Council consolidated lists; and OFAC SDN list as a U.S. clearing requirement. Screening is executed before name clearance and repeated at counterparty onboarding; enhanced due diligence and written risk rating are required for any non-resident or non-Canadian-source asset contributor.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises – Entreprise Registration and Search Portal (Québec)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name used by a limited partnership must be in French; a version in another language is permitted only when expressly authorized by the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The name must be written in Latin script using standard French diacritics; no ideographic or non-Latin script is accepted on the Quebec register. The proposed name must be distinct from existing names and must not create risk of confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal of a proposed name, the applicant files a written administrative reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the notice, including revised distinctive elements and authority evidence. If the reconsideration is refused, judicial or administrative review is available before the Tribunal administratif du Québec under the Act respecting administrative justice (CQLR c E-4.1) within 30 days. Reservations are not extendable; a fresh name-reservation application may be filed immediately after the prior 90-day window, and re-use of a refused name requires a materially different distinguishing element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole address for this industry. Refrigerated-logistics warehousing for perishable pharmaceuticals requires a physical, licensed, temperature-controlled storage establishment in Quebec; a virtual office cannot satisfy the commercial-substance requirement or the health and food-safety inspection regime. A virtual address may be used only for auxiliary correspondence in parallel with a real warehouse facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (75% estimated) - unannounced physical inspections are routine for cold-storage and pharmaceutical warehousing by Health Canada and provincial authorities; the LP must maintain continuous temperature logs, validated cold-chain equipment, and a designated responsible person on site.

Limited partnership declaration preparation and registration under CQLR c P-45
French-language compliance review of LP name and governing documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus consular/authentication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered establishment address (administrative correspondence directory) - 12 months

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cold-chain premises licensing and commercial-substance readiness pre-consultation (Health Canada / Quebec food safety)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory licensing tariff plus consultant market fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act (Loi sur les sociétés en commandite), CQLR c S-31.1, sections 2-12; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises), CQLR c P-44.1, sections 9-30
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Québec Enterprise Registrar, Québec, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. The limited partnership must have at least one general partner and one limited partner; capital contributions are fixed by the Limited Partnership Agreement and credited to each partner's capital account. Non-resident ownership is permitted, but the general partner must maintain a Québec address for service, and the partnership may be subject to Québec taxation based on its establishment in Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [•] LIMITED PARTNERSHIP, adopted pursuant to the Limited Partnership Act (Québec). The General Partner resolves as follows: (1) the capital subscriptions of the Limited Partners listed in Schedule A are accepted and their capital accounts are credited; (2) the registered office at [•], Province of Québec, as set out in the Declaration of Registration, is approved; (3) [•] is appointed Manager with sole authority to sign the Declaration, engage counsel and accountants, open Canadian bank accounts, file all regulatory declarations, and procure the Drug Establishment Licence; (4) the Manager is authorised to receive initial deposits by ACH direct and bank wire. This resolution took effect upon signing. Dated at Montréal, Québec, [•].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Name Search and Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the REQ enterprises register for identical or confusingly similar names; submit a name reservation request with a distinct legal element, distinctive element, and descriptive or activity element; if the name is non-distinctive, file a justification and obtain consent if required. Attach the reservation certificate to the declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Copy of completed name search results
Written power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, revise the distinctive element and re-submit; appeal the refusal to the inspector designated under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises within 60 days; use the exact name in the reservation certificate when filing the declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent legal counsel and, if applicable, a Québec notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a Limited Partnership Agreement among all general and limited partners stating capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management powers, and dissolution conditions. Prepare the Declaration of Registration under section 4 of the Limited Partnership Act; verify that all partners are identified, that the general partner has a Québec address for service, and that the statement of activities uses the NAICS 493120 code.
required_dossiers: Draft Declaration of Registration in prescribed form
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Identification and proof of address of each partner
Name reservation certificate from REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any inconsistency between the agreement and the declaration; re-execute signature pages; if the registrar queries the legal capacity of a partner, provide a certified translation or notarised identity documents and amend the declaration accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration electronically on the REQ platform; pay the statutory filing fee by credit card; upon validation, the limited partnership acquires legal personality by registration in the enterprise register. Download the Certificate of Registration (attestation d'immatriculation) issued by REQ.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Registration in prescribed form with original signatures
Name reservation certificate
Payment confirmation of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for insufficiency, the registry will issue a notice of defect; provide the missing information within 30 days; if the declaration is rejected, file a new declaration and pay any new fee; a refusal to register may be contested before the designated inspector and afterward before the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec - QST and Provincial Tax Registration Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN), then register for GST/HST and the Québec QST, and for payroll deduction accounts if employees will be hired. For the limited partnership, open the accounts in the partnership's legal name using the REQ certificate; associate the partners' social insurance or business numbers as required; receive the GST/HST and QST registration confirmations.
required_dossiers: REQ Certificate of Registration
Limited Partnership Agreement
Identification of each partner and of the general partner
Canadian bank account details for refund purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec flags a mismatch between the partnership name and partners' identifiers, submit a revised declaration and updated certificates; if an account is denied, file an objection with CRA or Revenu Québec and provide the partnership's registration certificate as proof of establishment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Drug Establishment Licensing Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Health Canada - Drug Licensing and Compliance Division (Québec Region); Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Drug Establishment Licence (DEL) for temporary and permanent cold storage and distribution of perishable pharmaceuticals; submit the required evidence of Good Distribution Practices, including temperature-mapped cold rooms, alarm systems, and batch-traceability SOPs. Concurrently apply to the RBQ for a certificate of conformity for the industrial building and register the workplace with CNESST.
required_dossiers: Drug Establishment Licence application in prescribed form
Site master file and quality manual
Temperature mapping and qualification reports for 2-8°C and -20°C chambers
RBQ building conformity application and structural plans
CNESST workplace registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Health Canada returns a deficiency letter, respond within 30 days with corrected SOPs or validation data; if RBQ refuses conformity, commission a structural engineer's report and resubmit; CNESST registrations are corrected by submitting a revised payroll and activities declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); Municipal Zoning and Building Services of the relevant Québec municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the refrigeration system type (anhydrous ammonia or halocarbon); for halocarbon systems file a declaration of conformity; for ammonia systems above the regulatory threshold apply for a certificate of authorisation under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act. Obtain a municipal zoning compliance certificate for the logistics warehouse and an occupancy permit for the refrigerated areas.
required_dossiers: Environmental declaration or certificate of authorisation application
Refrigerant inventory and leak-detection system details
Municipal zoning certificate
Building occupancy application for the cold-storage premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental filing is rejected, revise the technical sheets and resubmit; if the municipality denies the zoning certificate, either amend the declared activity to conform to the by-law or request a minor variance from the municipal council; any MELCCFP refusal may be appealed under the Environment Quality Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I chartered bank or Québec-based financial institution (e.g. BMO, RBC, National Bank, Desjardins)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a commercial bank account under the exact legal name of the limited partnership; present the REQ certificate, the partnership agreement, and the resolution of the general partner authorising the manager to operate the account; request ACH Direct and Bank Wire functionalities; pass the institution's KYC and AML review by providing source of funds and ultimate beneficial ownership details.
required_dossiers: REQ Certificate of Registration
Notarised or official copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement
General partner's resolution appointing the signatories
Personal identification and proof of address for all beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional AML documentation, provide consolidated ownership charts and source-of-wealth declarations; if the account application is refused, the partnership may apply to another financial institution without an additional regulatory filing, as the REQ registration is portable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada - Drug Licensing and Compliance Division; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Drug Establishment Licence (DEL) under the Food and Drug Regulations, C.02.014, authorising the storage and distribution of perishable pharmaceuticals under controlled temperature conditions, together with the RBQ certificate of conformity for the refrigerated warehouse premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Ministerial declaration of conformity for halocarbon refrigerant systems; full Certificate of Authorisation under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) required where anhydrous ammonia charge exceeds 500 kg or where the warehouse is located in a sensitive or densely populated zone
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Halocarbon systems must comply with the Règlement sur les halocarbures (CQLR c Q-2, r. 29): annual leak inspections, repair of leaks within 30 days, and recovery/reclamation of used refrigerants by an accredited operator; wastewater discharge into municipal sewers must respect municipal by-laws with typical limits of BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 600 mg/L, and pH between 6.0 and 9.5; emergency ammonia release must be vented through a permitted relief path and reported to MELCCFP under the emergency measures provisions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and occupancy permit from the local municipal fire safety service; compliance with the Québec Construction Code for structural loads, including high-bay racking and mezzanine floors; RBQ attestation confirming the cold storage building is safe for its intended use; CNESST occupational clearance covering, without limitation, emergency exit routes, ammonia sensor interlocks, personal protective equipment for refrigerated environments, and a written emergency response plan filed with the local fire department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Federal Fiscal Portal: Canada.ca Business Registration Online; for Quebec, Revenu Québec, Portal: revenuquebec.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity must register for a federal Business Number (BN) via the CRA's Business Registration Online or by filing Form RC1. For Quebec sales tax (QST), the partnership must register with Revenu Québec under the Quebec Business Number (NEQ) and obtain a QST registration number. The foreign general partner or designated Canadian representative must provide the LP agreement notarized/certified, proof of foreign registration, Quebec address for service, and identification of all partners for beneficial ownership. CRA BN and Revenu Québec QST registrations are mandatory before invoicing Canadian counterparties; specific accounts for GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM) are added to the BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: For Canadian federal tax purposes, a limited partnership is fiscally transparent and is not a separate taxpayer; each partner is allocated income/loss under the partnership agreement. However, the LP itself is required to file an information return (T5013) and to register for GST/HST/QST in respect of its Canadian commercial activities. The province of Quebec treats the LP as a pass-through for income tax, but imposes QST at the partnership level on taxable supplies made in Quebec; the LP is a registrant for QST purposes. The permanent establishment and territorial source rules apply to non-resident partners subject to Part XIV tax on Canadian-source business income, and withholding under Section 116 for dispositions of Canadian taxable property.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Partnership cannot elect to be taxed as a corporation under the Income Tax Act; however, for United States check-the-box purposes, the LP is a per se corporation if it is a Canadian entity organized as a limited partnership? Actually, Canadian LPs are generally not per se corporations for U.S. check-the-box; they can elect to be taxed as a corporation or partnership for U.S. purposes. Under Canadian hybrid mismatch rules (sections 12.8, 18.15, 18.2, 20.1), an eligible partnership can make a fiscal year-end election and a designated member election. Revenu Québec permits election for QST rebate on eligible capital property and joint elections under the Quebec Taxation Act mirroring federal provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) administered by CRA; Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec; the QST is a provincial tax harmonized in base with GST/HST but administered separately, plus customs duties/import taxes administered by CBSA
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Federal GST/HST: CAD 30,000 (taxable supplies worldwide); Quebec QST: CAD 30,000 (taxable supplies made in Quebec); a non-resident partnership with a Canadian permanent establishment is required to register for GST/HST regardless of the threshold; for QST, a non-resident carrying on business in Quebec must register regardless of threshold if it makes taxable supplies in Quebec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a national continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing clearance system; the CRA accepts XML/Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), Peppol interoperability, and PDF invoices. However, all GST/HST registrants must issue sales invoices containing prescribed information (vendor BN, date, description, tax rates, and amounts). Revenu Québec mandates that QST registrants issue prescribed invoices; as of 2023-2025, Quebec is gradually implementing mandatory electronic invoicing for B2B transactions in Quebec, with a phased mandate and future real-time reporting obligations under the Quebec government's e-invoicing roadmap (PEPPOL).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Taxable supplies of goods and services made by the LP qualify for GST/HST zero-rating when the goods are exported directly by the supplier or delivered to a recipient outside Canada, and for QST when goods are delivered outside Quebec/Canada, provided proof of export is retained. Cold storage warehouse services supplied to a non-resident recipient in respect of exported goods may be zero-rated where the service is performed on goods that are for export and the recipient is a non-resident. Interjurisdictional commercial cold storage services for perishable pharmaceuticals intended for export are eligible for zero-rating if the services are rendered directly in respect of exported goods. The LP must obtain documentary evidence of export within prescribed time limits; if title passes in Canada, domestic GST/HST applies unless the goods are exported under a continuous journey with proper customs documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Invoice (Form CI1), Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Export Declaration (Form B13A) or CADEX/CAED electronic export reporting
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill showing foreign destination
Commercial invoice with supplier BN/GST/HST registration number and zero-rating indication
Proof of payment and Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange contract or bank SWIFT confirmation
Signed written contract between the LP and the non-resident recipient
Packing list and transportation documents (truck/rail/ocean/air waybills)
CBSA-approved warehouse movement/export records for goods exiting via bonded or licensed cold storage facilities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the CRA or Revenu Québec audits and finds that the LP claimed zero-rating on goods/services not substantiated as exported, the LP is liable for uncollected GST/HST/QST, interest, and penalties. Under the Excise Tax Act, a 5% penalty plus interest applies to net tax deficiencies; Revenu Québec may impose a 15% penalty on a QST rebate/refund claim that is excessive, plus interest at the prescribed rate. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may constitute tax evasion under Section 239 of the Excise Tax Act / Sections 62 and 63 of the Quebec Tax Administration Act, leading to fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years. The CRA can deny input tax credits relating to the exported goods and reassess within the normal four-year limitation period (or ten years for misrepresentation).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada, with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervising Canadian-chartered banks and FINTRAC administering AML/ATF and cross-border transaction reporting. No separate foreign exchange control authority is vested with permitting powers in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII. Canada maintains no exchange controls, no capital-account restrictions and no requirement for prior central-bank approval on current or capital transfers. Trade invoicing, service remittances, partner capital calls, interest, dividends and profit distributions may flow freely into and out of Canada. The sole legal friction for profit remittance from a Quebec LP is tax-driven: non-resident partners may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax on Canadian-source allocations or distributions under the Canadian Income Tax Act, and Revenu Québec may impose provincial withholding. The remitting bank will require tax identification, TP106/NR4 documentation, and a completed certificate of compliance where cross-border dividend-equivalent or partnership income is being paid.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any export proceeds surrender timeline, mandatory conversion percentage, or repatriation requirement. Export proceeds from cold-storage and logistics services may be held in foreign currency in Canadian banks or remitted in the invoiced currency. However, any physical or monetary instrument movement exceeding CAD 10,000 crossing the Canadian border must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency and FINTRAC; the underlying commercial contracts, GL001 export declarations and customs documentation must be maintained for statutory retention periods.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. An offshore digital electronic money institution (EMI) may not act as a primary domicile for the settlement account of a Quebec LP unless it is registered with FINTRAC as a Money Service Business under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and, where it provides retail payment services in Canada, holds authorization from the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Unlicensed offshore EMIs cannot send CAD via Payments Canada clearing rails, have no access to CDIC-insured settlement, and will not be accepted as the main treasury counterparty by tier-1 supply chain partners. Viability improves only if the EMI provides a prepaid or pass-through card solely to a licensed Canadian schedule-I bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorized director, general partner, or senior corporate officer is de facto mandatory for a first-time non-resident Quebec LP. Canadian AML interpretation of FINTRAC's identity verification standards allows video-verified identity checks, but Quebec banks generally require one retrospective in-person interview at the account-opening branch or through a notarized alternative with apostille. Non-resident limited partners may be onboarded via remote documentary KYC only if the General Partner performs the physical attendance, the LP is registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, and all UBO documentation is certified. An authorized local agent with power of attorney is often accepted only after the Bank's compliance committee deliberates the low-risk-rated cold-storage operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex partnership cap table with non-resident partners in mixed roles and indirect UBO interests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of DECLARATION OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP filed with Registraire des entreprises du Québec; full UBO organisational chart with percentage attribution; LP agreement; capital call notices; notarized statements of source of wealth and source of funds; passport copies and proof of residential address for all beneficial owners holding 10% or more; tax self-certification under CRS/FATCA for each non-resident partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value disbursements for perishable pharmaceutical cold-storage without visible trade-backing documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client warehouse service agreements; temperature-monitoring and chain-of-custody records; issued warehouse receipts; customs B3/CBSA declarations; supplier purchase orders and delivery confirmations; GST/QST remittance records; annual or reviewed interim financial statements; CRA-registered business number and employer registrations; summary of the physical facility lease and ISO 13485 / GDP certification if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital transfers from jurisdictions listed on Canada's high-risk or sanctioned territories list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters from the remitting financial institution; corporate certificate of good standing; beneficial ownership declaration; copies of underlying capital-call agreements and the commercial reality of a Quebec refrigerated warehouse; FATCA/CRS declaration forms; explanation letter mapping the commercial flow from limited partner capital into construction, refrigeration equipment, or working capital; confirmation that the partnership does not transact in prohibited currency or with restricted counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound partner capital contributions should be made by SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the LP's capital escrow or operational account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The remittance must include the payment purpose clearly identified in field 70 as 'PARTNERSHIP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION UNDER LP AGREEMENT DATED YYYY-MM-DD' and must reference the specific capital call number. Domestic and cross-border wire settlement occurs through Payments Canada Lynx for immediate CAD clearing or through correspondent USD settlement networks for foreign currency. If the capital amount exceeds CAD 10,000 in cash or monetary instruments, a FINTRAC cross-border currency report is triggered. No foreign-exchange approval certificate or Canadian Ministry of Finance authorization is required for capital injection. Supporting records must include the executed capital call, subscription/contribution schedule, and bank confirmation statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operating disbursements for the cold-storage warehouse are cleared using Payments Canada Lynx and EFT/ACH rails for domestic CAD obligations, while cross-border supplier payments in USD, EUR, GBP or CHF are routed through SWIFT MT103 wires with ISO 20022 structured remittance data. Standard commercial open-account payment is acceptable under low-risk supply chain terms; where suppliers require smoothing of default risk, issuance of commercial documentary letters of credit (L/C) under UCP 600 with confirmed SWIFT MT700 series is permissible for capital-equipment purchases such as refrigeration compressors or pharmaceutical cold-chain vehicles. Canada does not require submission of import permits for most temperature-controlled logistics goods; however, import controls under Health Canada and cGMP documentation may be required for pharma-adjacent materials. The LP's treasury operations must maintain full supporting files for CRA and Revenu Québec in case a cross-border PAYMENT is challenged as non-commercial or exceptional-purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/CAD FX forward contracts executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-liquidity emerging-market currency exposures, settled in USD or CAD on a net basis through a licensed Schedule I bank
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) used to match non-resident partners' foreign-currency capital inflows with long-dated CAD or USD trade disbursement requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the enterprise to the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Government of Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 60th day following the registration anniversary date of the limited partnership (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, s. 32); if the 60th day falls on a non-juridical day, filing is extended to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 100 (approx. USD 74) in addition to the CAD 20 base fee; continued non-filing triggers a REQ notice of intention to strike off; if the partnership does not respond within 30 days after the notice, its registration is struck from the enterprise register, resulting in loss of legal capacity to carry on business or enforce contracts in Quebec and joint liability of the general partner for obligations incurred after strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal partnership information return and annual partner allocation slips (T5013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business and Income Tax Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T5013 return due within 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); T5013 slips must be distributed to partners and filed with CRA no later than March 31 following the calendar year in which the fiscal period ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and failure-to-file penalties under Income Tax Act s. 162: CAD 25 per day per slip/return, up to CAD 2,500, escalating to CAD 100 per day up to CAD 25,000 for gross negligence or repeat failures; CRA may also assess a failure-to-report penalty of 5% of the amount that should have been reported, plus 1% per month up to 12 months, and prescribed interest on any partner-level reassessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership income return (TP-1064) of the partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); the fiscal period for Quebec tax purposes must match the federal fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under the Taxation Act (Quebec): 5% of any amount payable by the partnership plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months (increased for repeated delinquencies), with prescribed-rate interest; willful non-filing is punishable by additional administrative penalties and, in serious cases, by penal prosecution of the managing general partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on Quebec limited partnerships by the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An independent audit becomes compulsory when: (i) the partnership agreement requires audited financial statements; (ii) a lender or institutional lessee contractually requires audited statements; (iii) the limited partnership is consolidated by a reporting issuer or public sector entity; or (iv) Health Canada's Drug Establishment Licence or Good Storage Practices regime conditions the storage licence on annual third-party facility audits for temperature-controlled pharmaceutical warehousing
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Privately held Canadian limited partnerships generally prepare financial statements in accordance with Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) – CPA Canada Handbook Part II; IFRS (Part I) applies only if the partnership is a publicly accountable enterprise or voluntarily elects IFRS. CRA and Revenu Québec accept ASPE statements with book-to-tax reconciliations; fiscal records must be sufficient to support all income and expense allocations among general and limited partners

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec currently imposes no annual UBO (beneficial ownership) confirmation for limited partnerships; the public enterprise register records only general partners. Each annual declaration to the REQ implicitly attests that the recorded general-partner particulars are current. Transfers of limited partnership interests are documented internally in the register of limited partners and reflected in the annual T5013 / RL-15 allocation slips; a change of a general partner must be filed with REQ within 15 days of the change. Limited partners' capital balances and profit-sharing ratios should be reconfirmed by the managing general partner annually in a partner resolution; no government filing of limited-partner identities is required
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners (names, domicile, contributions, withdrawals)
Register of Limited Partners (capital accounts, contribution dates, assignment history, allocation ratios)
Minute Book of General Partner Resolutions (annual confirmations, distributions, indemnity, authority delegations)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220–1,100 per annum (CAD 300–1,500) for a Quebec registered office address and corporate agent, depending on location and mail-forwarding services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,700–14,700 (CAD 5,000–20,000) for a contracted certified audit or agreed-upon-procedures engagement covering the partnership's annual financial statements and cold-chain storage records, when required by the partnership agreement, a lender, or Health Canada conditions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the limited partnership level (fiscally transparent); corporate partners are subject to a combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) headline corporate rate of 26.5% on allocated taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday for refrigerated logistics warehousing. The LP itself is not taxable; partners may benefit from flow-through of federal and Quebec SR&ED tax credits, investment tax credits, and the Quebec innovation tax credit. The federal small business deduction is generally unavailable to an LP and is limited to a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner on active business income subject to its passive income thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return filed through CRA EFILE/TELEFILE at canada.ca; Quebec ancillary Declarations and RL-15 slips filed through Revenu Quebec's Mon Dossier d'Entreprise portal; federal T106 Information Return for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions may also be required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than six months after the partnership fiscal period end; for a calendar-year LP, the federal T5013 and Quebec equivalent are due by June 30 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a — Partnership legal name and business number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the limited partnership, CRA business number (BN), Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), and address of the principal establishment in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should be identified in the partnership's records by full legal name, tax treaty residence, and Canadian agent details; the BN must be the active Quebec permanent establishment code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: End date of the LP's fiscal period, which normally follows the fiscal period of the majority of partners or as elected under ITA s. 249.1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident partner has a different taxation year, the LP's allocation to that partner is determined based on the partnership fiscal period and must be reported consistently with the partner's Canadian return obligations under s. 216.1 ITA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 — Partner allocation of income, losses, and other amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's proportionately allocated share of the LP's cold-storage business revenues, deductible expenses, capital cost allowance, and restricted farm or non-capital losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations to non-resident partners are taxable in Canada under ss. 2(3.1), 115, and 216.1 ITA; the partner's country of residence code and treaty relief position must be annotated and the responsible partner must retain the certificate of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed gross revenue and expense breakdown for the refrigerated warehousing operation (NAICS 493120), including storage fees, utilities, inventory shrinkage, spoilage, and cold-chain equipment costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expense allocations must comply with arm's-length standards and be supported by contemporaneous documentation; cross-border recharges to or from non-resident related parties must be identified on the T106 information return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec client copy reporting the annual income or loss allocated to each resident and non-resident partner for the LP's fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner without a Quebec permanent establishment is still required to receive the RL-15 and may need to file a Quebec income tax return if subject to Part I Quebec tax on allocated net income; treaty relief must be claimed through the federal filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the T5013 or Quebec LP return attracts a CRA penalty of $100 plus $25 per day of delay, to a maximum of $2,500; repeated failures can trigger higher penalties and a formal demand before prosecution under the Excise Tax Act / Quebec Tax Administration Act. Non-resident partner information slip failures also carry per-slip penalties and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax applies to dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident person; ordinary profit allocations by a limited partnership are not treated as dividends but are taxable to the partner under Part I/Part XIV of the ITA, subject to treaty allocation and TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must provide the payer with a signed Form NR301 (Residence for Tax Purposes) and a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the home treaty jurisdiction before the payment is made. If the payer withholds at the statutory rate in error, the non-resident files a refund claim with CRA (Form NR7-R or the appropriate T5013/T5 slip review) within two years, attaching the TRC and treaty analysis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory Part XIII rates are 25% for non-resident royalties and 25% for non-resident interest unless the interest is made to an arm's-length Canadian payer and is exempt under ITA s. 212(1)(b)(i)(C). Most Canadian tax treaties reduce royalties to 10% and interest to 0% or 15%; Quebec does not levy an independent withholding tax on cross-border payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CA$1,000,000 — when the total annual value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with a non-resident related person exceeds CA$1 million, the LP must prepare, keep, and provide contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation under ITA s. 247(4), including a master file, local file, risk assessment, and functional analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada is not a designated ESR jurisdiction; however, CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under s. 245 ITA and interprets economic substance as a critical factor. A Quebec limited partnership operating in cold storage must maintain physical premises, employees, management, and real commercial activity; a shell that exists solely for treaty/conduit access will be reassessed and penalised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully or through gross negligence omitting cold-storage revenues, inflating management fees, fabricating inventory spoilage claims, or making false entries in the T5013 to shift taxable profits from the Quebec LP to a non-resident partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s. 239(1) carries a fine of 100% to 200% of the tax evaded and incarceration up to 5 years; civil gross-negligence penalty under ITA s. 163(2) is 50% of the understated tax; Quebec Revenu imposes parallel administrative and criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and directors of a corporate partner are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/QST under ITA s. 323 and the Quebec Taxation Act; a conviction triggers travel bans, asset seizures, and potential extradition for deceitful tax conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Quebec LP as a letterbox with no employees, no significant premises, and no management substance while invoicing cross-border cold-storage services from Quebec to related offshore entities to avoid Canadian Part I tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterizes the arrangement and imposes tax, interest, and a 25% gross-negligence penalty; Revenu Quebec may deregister the LP and deny refunds; the arrangement can be prosecuted as a sham for tax evasion if deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, promoters, and designated partners are personally assessed for the tax that would otherwise have been collectible; a criminal conviction can result in prohibition from acting as a director, travel bans, and civil restitution for unpaid taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct FINTRAC-mandated beneficial-owner due diligence on large non-resident cash clients, or knowingly processing warehousing payments that conceal the proceeds of crime, despite the low inherent AML risk tier of the cold-storage industry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for non-compliance with client identification, record-keeping, and reporting; criminal laundering charges carry fines of up to $2,000,000 and imprisonment for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are individually liable for failure to file FINTRAC reports and can be imprisoned up to 5 years for laundering funds; travel restrictions, a seven-year border inquiry, and mandatory reporting of the Canadian criminal record apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's-length cross-border management, rental, royalty, or logistics service arrangements between the Quebec LP and foreign related parties without contemporaneous TP documentation or at prices that deviate from the arm's-length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjusts taxable income under ITA s. 247(2) and imposes a 10% transfer-pricing penalty under s. 247(3) on the net adjustment, plus interest and potential gross-negligence penalties; failure to file the T106 return attracts $100/day penalties up to $2,500.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for the resulting Canadian and Quebec taxes and penalties; sustained evasion exposure may trigger CRA criminal referral, travel bans, and civil claims by aggrieved creditors.
